text: . India and Lebanon have reviewed the entire gamut of bilateral relations and discussed ways to further strengthen it across political-security, economic and socio-cultural pillars. The first India-Lebanon Foreign Office Consultations was held at New Delhi yesterday. It was co-chaired by Secretary (CPV & OIA) in External Affairs Ministry, Sripriya Ranganathan and Secretary-General of lebanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants, Abdel Sattar Issa.Both sides identified cooperation in trade and investment, digital public infrastructure and pharmaceuticals, as priorities. They also discussed regional and international issues of mutual interest. Both countries share warm and cordial bilateral relations, across the pillars of Political, Economic and Cultural domains. External Affairs Ministry said that the discussions held today will contribute in further strengthening of India-Lebanon bilateral partnership.

. The depression, a remnant of Cyclone Arnab, over south Chhattisgarh and adjoining south Odisha has moved northwards.It is now centred over central Chhattisgarh and adjoining Odisha. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) said it is likely to move further north and weaken into a well-marked low-pressure area over north Chhattisgarh tonight.Meanwhile, IMD has issued a red alert for very heavy to extremely heavy rainfall in Bihar tomorrow.An orange alert has been issued for very heavy rainfall in East Uttar Pradesh, Sub-Himalayan West Bengal, Sikkim and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands tomorrow. Heavy rainfall is also expected in Jharkhand and Uttarakhand.Thunderstorms accompanied by hail are likely over East Rajasthan, Haryana, Chandigarh, Uttarakhand and West Uttar Pradesh.Thunderstorms and gusty winds are also forecast in several other states, including Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Punjab, Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Assam and Meghalaya.Meanwhile Delhi witnessed light to moderate rainfall this evening. The IMD has forecast very light rain accompanied by thunderstorms and lightning tomorrow morning.The maximum temperature is expected to remain between 26 and 28 degrees Celsius, while the minimum temperature is likely to range from 16 to 18 degrees Celsius.

. India’s water management initiatives have emerged as a model for developing countries. World Bank Global Director for Water, Saroj Kumar Jha, has described India’s progress as a remarkable success story. Speaking ahead of the 2026 United Nations Water Conference, Mr Jha praised initiatives such as the Jal Jeevan Mission, Namami Gange and Swachh Bharat Mission. He said the Jal Jeevan Mission had provided improved drinking water access to 800 million people in less than seven years. He also lauded efforts to clean the Ganga and strengthen the safety of nearly 900 dams. Mr Jha urged India to share its experiences globally at the conference, scheduled in Abu Dhabi from December 8 to 10.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said that India is now home to a hundred chess Grandmasters. Congratulating Anuj Shrivatri on becoming India’s 100th Chess Grandmaster, the Prime Minister said that India’s reaching 100 Grandmasters is a remarkable milestone that reflects the immense talent, dedication and hard work of Indian players as well as the growing popularity of chess among the youth. In a social media post, he also expressed delight that young chess talents emerging from different parts of the country are making their mark on the global stage. Mr Modi expressed hope that the achievement will inspire many more youngsters to take up chess and pursue excellence.

. Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Ryabkov has said that Moscow has no intention, plans or reason to attack any European country. Addressing an OSCE roundtable discussion on the militarisation of Europe, Ryabkov said Western countries were portraying a military conflict in Europe as almost inevitable. He warned that Russia would be forced to respond if subjected to aggression. He also accused some European governments of lacking genuine commitment to ending the Russia-Ukraine conflict. Ryabkov expressed hope that Europe would eventually resume dialogue with Moscow based on equality, mutual respect and security interests. He stressed that lasting peace in Europe must take Russia’s interests into account.

. The government today launched the sixth edition of the National Startup Awards to recognise outstanding startups across the country. The awards recognise not just commercial success but also social impact, sustainability, and scalability. Launching the awards in New Delhi today, DPIIT Secretary Amardeep Singh said that startups can apply under 20 sectoral categories. He said that in addition, there are three special categories for women, students, and the North Eastern region. He added that the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade is at the forefront of driving reforms to promote startups. Mr Singh also emphasised the need for more private initiative to bring more startups in the country. He expressed hope that the awards would further boost the startup ecosystem in the country. The Secretary highlighted that the award covers a wide range of domains including agriculture, fintech, aerospace, health, education, and accessibility, among others. The applications for the award will remain open until 20 November this year.In line with the Government’s vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat and the goal of a five-trillion-dollar economy, Startup India supports startups through initiatives such as startup recognition, tax exemptions, regulatory ease, funding access, and capacity building. Launched in 2016, Startup India has transformed India’s entrepreneurial landscape, fostering innovation and empowering youth, women, students, and first-time founders, particularly from Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities. Over two lakh 25 thousand startups have been recognised by DPIIT so far.

. In ODI men’s cricket, India defeated New Zealand by four runs under the Duckworth-Lewis-Stern (DLS) method following a rain stoppage at the Hnry Stadium in Wellington today. India were 113 for seven in 26 overs, and needed 22 runs from 66 balls when play was called off.Batting first, New Zealand were bowled out for 134 following a disastrous outing in rainy Wellington. India won the first ODI of the five-match series by five wickets, and now leads the rubber 2-nil.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi today extended greetings on the occasion of Gujarati New Year. In a social media post, the Prime Minister expressed hope that this fresh start brings new hopes of happiness, peace, prosperity, and well-being into everyone’s lives. Mr Modi also prayed that everyone’s life remains filled with excellent health, enthusiasm, and zeal.

. Union Culture and Tourism Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat today highlighted that India’s civilizational consciousness will offer valuable guidance in dealing with present day challenges in the country. The Minister stated this at the book launch of Timeless India: Protection and Revival of Indian Cultural Identity under the leadership of the Prime Minister in New Delhi. Mr Shekhawat said that this book offers a unique perspective on the initiatives undertaken by the government to safeguard and revive India’s rich cultural heritage. He emphasised that preserving and revitalising this legacy is essential not only for safeguarding the country’s historical identity but also for shaping its future.This book is written by Former Rajya Sabha Member Tarun Vijay and  published by Indira Gandhi National Centre of Arts and Surbhi publication.

. Vice-President C P Radhakrishnan has greeted everyone on the occasion of Govardhan Puja. In a social media post, the Vice-President prayed that Lord Krishna bless every home with happiness, peace, prosperity and positivity. Mr Radhakrishnan wished that the festival strengthen the values of devotion, gratitude and togetherness.

. In Tennis, India’s Vaishnavi Adkar and Rutuja Bhosale will aim to create history when they take on Switzerland’s Naima Karamoko and Simona Waltert in the women’s doubles final of the WTA tournament at SDAT Tennis Stadium, Chennai, this evening.The Indian pair will become the first all-Indian team to contest a WTA Tour-level doubles final, with the title clash scheduled to begin at 4 p.m. IST. Adkar and Bhosale booked their place in the final after defeating second seeds Weronika Falkowska and Alana Smith 6-2, 2-6, [10-8] in a thrilling semifinal yesterday.A victory would mark a significant milestone for Indian women’s tennis, as Adkar and Bhosale look to cap their memorable campaign with a historic WTA doubles crown.

. India and the United States have reaffirmed commitment to strengthen bilateral counter-narcotics cooperation towards ensuring the safety and well-being of their communities. The reaffirmation came during the two-day 2nd India-U.S. Drug Policy Executive Working Group Meeting held in New Delhi last week.According to a joint press release issued by Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB), the meeting reviewed bilateral cooperation in combatting illicit drug trafficking and identified priority areas for strengthening intelligence sharing, coordinated law enforcement action, pharmaceutical supply chain integrity, and drug demand reduction. Director General, NCB, Anurag Garg led the Indian delegation and the U.S. delegation was headed by Acting Deputy Director, Office of National Drug Control Policy (ONDCP), Debbie Seguin during the meeting. In his opening remarks, Mr Garg highlighted the India Vision Roadmap 2026-2029 which outlines a comprehensive strategy to combat the illicit narcotics trade. DG NCB also highlighted India’s adoption of a network-centric approach to decisively dismantle drug trafficking networks by targeting their entire ecosystem, including financiers, suppliers, facilitators and logistical networks.ONDCP Director Sara Carter highlighted that the bilateral cooperation between the United States and India is vital to disrupting transnational drug trafficking networks and preventing the diversion of synthetic drugs and chemical precursors into global markets. She emphasized that the strategy must be equally targeted, and said that both countries must partner across borders to secure the commercial supply chains they exploit.

. Indian pacer Mohammed Shami has announced his retirement from Test cricket, bringing the curtain down on his 13-year career in the longest format of the game. However, he will continue to represent India in limited-overs cricket. Shami announced his decision in a social media post. He finished his Test career with 229 wickets from 64 matches at an average of 27.71, including six five-wicket hauls.The 36-year-old fast bowler ended his career as India’s sixth-highest wicket-taking fast bowler in Test cricket, behind Kapil Dev, Zaheer Khan, Ishant Sharma, Javagal Srinath and Jasprit Bumrah. With this announcement, Shami brings an end to a significant chapter in his international career while keeping his focus on the shorter formats of the game.

. The Gujarati community across the world is celebrating New Year, popularly known as ‘Bestu Varsh’, today. It is marked by the first day of the Kartik month in the Vikram Samvat calendar.On this occasion, Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel, and Union Home Minister Amit Shah will exchange New Year greetings with the people. Akashvani correspondent reports that the New Year begins with the sacred tradition of seeking divine blessings. From early morning, temples across the state are witnessing huge footfalls as people start their day with prayers for a year filled with peace and prosperity.It is also a vibrant social day, with people visiting the residences of near and dear ones to exchange heartfelt greetings of ‘Nutan Varshabhinandan’-Happy New Year-accompanied by traditional sweets.In the commercial sphere, traders and business houses are performing the ceremonial worship of their new account books, known as Chopda Poojan, to seek the blessings of Goddess Lakshmi for financial success in the year ahead. Tomorrow, the festive cycle will continue with the observance of Bhai Bij, celebrating family bonds.

. Delhi Government has declared a holiday on the 16th of this month (Monday) on account of Chhath Puja. All Government offices, Autonomous Bodies and Public Sector Undertakings of the NCT of Delhi will remain closed on the day as per a notification issued by the General Administration Department.

. Wall Street ended on a mixed note yesterday. The Nasdaq Composite climbed 1.1 per cent as investors returned to AI-related and chip stocks after the recent sell-off, while the S&P 500 gained 0.3 per cent. Conversely, the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell half a per cent.All three major indices posted losses for the week. The Nasdaq lost 3.4 per cent, the S&P 500 dropped 2.7 per cent and the Dow slipped 0.9 per cent.On the economic front, the US labour market strengthened in October. Nonfarm payrolls rose by 1 lakh 65 thousand, while the unemployment rate fell marginally to 4.1 per cent from 4.2 per cent in September, according to the data released by the US Bureau of Labour Statistics.

. In Bangladesh, Kali Puja, also known as Shyama Puja, was celebrated across Bangladesh with religious fervour, devotion and enthusiasm. Devotees gathered at temples and makeshift mandaps to offer prayers to Goddess Kali and mark the triumph of good over evil.Popularly known as Deepawali or the festival of lights, Kali Puja is observed on the new moon night of the Bengali month of Kartik. The festival honours Goddess Kali, regarded as the embodiment of divine power, strength and the destruction of evil.As part of the celebrations, devotees illuminated their homes, temples and crematoriums with earthen lamps and candles in remembrance of their ancestors. Special prayers, traditional rituals, devotional music and offerings marked the occasion.In the capital, major celebrations took place at Dhakeshwari National Temple, Ramkrishna Math and Mission, Siddheshwari Kali Mandir, Ramna Kali Mandir and several other religious sites.The Ramna Kali Mandir was particularly illuminated with lamps and decorative lights, while devotees gathered to offer prayers. Fireworks also added to the festive atmosphere.Celebrations were also reported in divisional cities, including Chattogram, and district towns such as Jashore.

. On World Immunization Day today, Union Health Minister Jagat Prakash Nadda renewed the country’s commitment to protecting every child and pregnant women through timely and complete immunisation. In a social media post, the Minister said that India’s achievements in eliminating polio and maternal and neonatal tetanus reflects the impact of sustained immunisation efforts. Mr Nadda highlighted initiatives like the Universal Immunization Programme, U-WIN digital platform and Mission Indradhanush campaign and said these are expanding access to life-saving vaccines. He reiterated that every dose counts and added that no child or pregnant women should be left unprotected.

. Global crude oil prices declined today. Brent crude was trading three and a half per cent down at 94 US dollars and 92 cents per barrel. West Texas Intermediate crude was trading 2.8 per cent lower at 87 US dollars and seven cents per barrel, when reports last came in.

. External Affair Minister Dr S Jaishankar spoke with Russia’s Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov over phone yesterday evening. In a social media post, Dr Jaishankar said that their conversation focused on the Ukraine conflict and ongoing diplomatic initiatives. The two leaders also discussed current issues of Russia-India cooperation, as well as relevant regional and international affairs.

. The Department of Pension and Pensioners’ Welfare will conduct the month-long fifth nation-wide Digital Life Certificate (DLC) campaign across the country from the 1st of next month. Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions Ministry said that this is the biggest-ever DLC Campaign undertaken by the Ministry. Electronics and Information Technology Ministry and UIDAI will provide technical support during this campaign. The Ministry said that the initiative will be adopted with a Whole of Government approach with the objective of reaching pensioners in the remotest corners of the country with focus on Face Authentication Technology. The Ministry said that face Authentication for Digital Life Certificate is a seamless and fast mode for DLC generation which can be used both on Android and Apple devices, making it easy and convenient for elderly Pensioners.The Campaign will be conducted in an Utsav mode by offering a bouquet of services such as Health Check-ups and Aadhaar updation for pensioners. Doorstep services to be provided to pensioners based on their requirement.

. In tennis, India’s Vaishnavi Adkar and Rutuja Bhosale finished runners-up in the women’s doubles at the WTA 250 Chennai Open today. The Indian pair lost 2-6, 0-6 to Switzerland’s Simona Waltert and Naima Karamoko in the final.Despite the defeat in the title clash, Adkar and Bhosale made history by becoming the first all-Indian pair to reach a WTA Tour-level doubles final.Yesterday in the semifinals, the Indian duo defeated second seeds Weronika Falkowska and Alana Smith 6-2, 2-6, [10-8] to move into the final.

. India and Saudi Arabia have signed the bilateral Haj agreement for 2027, under which 1 lakh 75 thousand 25 Indians will be allowed to undertake the annual pilgrimage. Union Minority Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju, who is on an official visit to Saudi Arabia, held a bilateral meeting with Saudi Minister of Hajj and Umrah Tawfiq bin Fawzan Al Rabiah before signing the agreement in Jeddah. The Ministers reviewed the ongoing preparations for Haj-2027, discussed measures to strengthen bilateral coordination and logistical support, and reaffirmed their shared commitment to a safe, smooth and comfortable pilgrimage for Indian Haj pilgrims. Saudi Arabia sets annual Haj quotas for countries to regulate the number of pilgrims visiting Mecca, as space and facilities at the holy sites are limited.

. The Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) and the National Stock Exchange (NSE) will remain closed tomorrow on account of Diwali-Balipratipada. Trading or settlement activities will remain suspended across market segments including equities, equity derivatives, and currency derivatives. However, the commodity segment will observe a partial trading holiday. The Multi Commodity Exchange (MCX) will remain closed during the morning session but will resume trading in the evening session from 5:00 PM onwards.

. In shooting, India’s Niveditha Veloor Nair secured a bronze medal in the women’s 25-metre standard pistol at the ISSF World Championship in Doha, Qatar, yesterday. Niveditha finished third with a score of 567-13x.China’s Xiao Jiaruixuan won gold while Hungary’s Veronika Major claimed silver with. India’s Manvi Jain and Simranpreet Kaur Brar finished eighth and 10th, respectively.In the team event, the Indian trio of Niveditha Nair, Manvi Jain and Simranpreet Kaur Brar secured silver with a combined score of 1,682-33x. With this, India’s overall tally at the Doha championship has risen to seven, comprising one gold, five silver and one bronze.

. Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta will distribute free LPG cylinders to eligible families today. The grant amount will be transferred directly into beneficiaries’ bank accounts through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT). Food and Supplies Minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa will also attend the event. Earlier, spokespersons for the ruling BJP hit out at the AAP for doing politics over stubble burning incidents in Punjab and deterioration in air quality in north India.

. Russia battered Ukraine’s power grid again and Ukrainian forces hit another of Russia’s biggest oil refineries hours before delegations from Moscow and Kyiv were due to meet for new US-brokered talks to end the ongoing crisis. Russian, Ukrainian and US negotiators are set to hold two-day talks in Abu Dhabi from tomorrow, marking their first meeting since February.Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov today said that US President Donald Trump’s team has placed collective security covering not just Russia and Ukraine but also a wider area at the top of the agenda for the two days of discussions.Security guarantees are expected to dominate the discussions, amid continuing hostilities and intensified missile and drone attacks by both sides. Russia is demanding territorial concessions from Ukraine and an end to its NATO membership demand. However, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has rejected these conditions, insisting on a ceasefire and firm security guarantees against future aggression. The United States is seeking practical arrangements to address the security concerns of all parties. Meanwhile, European participation remains contentious, with Moscow opposing their involvement at this stage.During five years of the conflict, the two countries remain locked in battle with no sign that either side is ready to budge from their demands. US President Donald Trump said in an interview that aired last Sunday that Moscow and Kyiv are very close to a deal.

. In men’s cricket, India suffered a three-wicket defeat to Pakistan in their Group A clash of the ACC Men’s Under-19 Asia Cup in Oman this evening.Batting first, India were bowled out for 208, powered by Arjun Rajput’s 107 off 85 balls. For Pakistan, Rizwanullah, Ali Raza, and Niqab Shafiq each picked up three wickets.In reply, Pakistan chased down the target, losing seven wickets in 48.1 overs, with the help of Hamza Zahoor’s unbeaten 100 off 108 balls. For India, Manal Chauhan took three wickets, while Mohit Ulva scalped two.Earlier, India had won the toss and elected to bat first.

. United States, Ukraine and Russia will begin two-day talks in Abu Dhabi today to end Ukraine conflict. Mediated by Washington, this meeting marks the first formal three-way discussion since negotiations were suspended in February this year. According to US Special Envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff, who are leading the American delegation, the primary focus of the session is defining a post-war security architecture to guarantee that once a ceasefire is reached, the conflict does not reignite.The talks aim to expand the conversation from strict territorial boundaries to a broader framework of European and regional security. Other immediate priorities include practical de-escalation measures along the current frontline, urgent humanitarian aid distributions and expanded prisoner exchanges and structuring international aid for Ukraine’s post-war economic reconstruction.The greatest obstacle remains the fundamental definition of peace. Russian President Vladimir Putin continues to demand that Ukraine permanently cede four annexed regions, dramatically downsize its standing military, and formally abandon its bid to join NATO. Conversely, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has firmly rejected any forced capitulation or territorial concessions that compromise Ukraine’s sovereignty, demanding ironclad security guarantees akin to NATO’s Article 5 protection against future invasions.Furthermore, while the Kremlin has insisted that the talks remain strictly trilateral to exclude European powers, representatives from European Union nations, the UK, France, Germany, and NATO are also in Abu Dhabi to conduct parallel, separate coordination meetings with the Ukrainian delegation.

. The COP31 climate summit has started in Turkey today. World leaders at the meeting urged countries to act much faster to stop global warming, warning that the climate crisis is getting worse. Even though the world is currently facing other major problems like wars, rising prices, and the rapid growth of artificial intelligence, leaders emphasized that protecting the planet must remain a top priority.UN Climate Change Executive Secretary Simon Stiell warned that current progress is far too slow, a concern underscored by a UN report showing that the world is on track to overshoot the critical 1.5°C warming threshold. Driven by a powerful El Niño, 2026 is shaping up to be one of the hottest years on record, marked by severe heatwaves in Western Europe and a catastrophic glacier collapse in Nepal that killed over 1,450 people.

. The Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) and National Stock Exchange (NSE) conducted muhurat trading on the occasion of Diwali, marking the beginning of Samvat 2083. Benchmark domestic equity indices ended today’s special trading session in the negative zone. The Sensex ended marginally lower by 29 points to close at 80 thousand 999, while the Nifty dipped 44 points, or 0.18 per cent to settle at 24 thousand 986. Conversely, the broader market on the National Stock Exchange ended with gains. The Midcap 100 index rose over 0.1 per cent, while the Smallcap 100 index jumped one per cent.

. Most Asian stock markets ended on a mixed note today. South Korea’s Kospi fell 0.8 per cent, Singapore’s Strait Times index declined 2.2 per cent and Hong Kong’s Hang Seng edged down marginally. Conversely, Japan’s Nikkei 225 climbed over 2.3 per cent, Taiwan’s Taiex rose nearly five per cent and China’s Shanghai Composite gained 0.3 per cent.In European markets, Germany’s DAX rose nearly one per cent, and London’s FTSE 100 gained 0.8 per cent, when reports last came in.

. Akashvani will broadcast the recording of the annual Sardar Patel Memorial Lecture, delivered by Agriculture and Farmers Welfare Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan, tonight at 9:30 PM. The recording will be broadcast across the entire Akashvani network on the occasion of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel’s birth anniversary.Delivering the 67th Sardar Patel Memorial Lecture, Mr Chouhan said that Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel’s vision, determination and leadership laid the foundation for India’s national unity and territorial integrity. He said that Sardar Patel’s efforts to integrate 565 princely states remain a defining chapter in the country’s history. The Minister emphasised that Patel’s vision of a united India continues to inspire the nation through the spirit of ‘Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat’.Mr Chouhan also said that, inspired by Sardar Patel’s firm approach towards national security and his policy of zero tolerance towards terrorism, India has responded decisively to threats from across its borders, including through measures such as surgical strikes.As a tribute to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, who served as independent India’s first Deputy Prime Minister and Information and Broadcasting Minister, Akashvani has been organising the annual Sardar Patel Memorial Lecture since 1955. Over the years, the annual event has served as a rich repository of thoughts, ideas and perspectives on a wide range of subjects. It has also provided an opportunity to gain a deeper understanding of India’s diverse cultural heritage and the various dimensions of its developmental challenges.

. Indian Railways has geared up to manage the ongoing festive season rush of Diwali and Chhath Puja, with extensive crowd management preparations underway at several railway stations. Ministry of Railways said that Indian Railways is developing dedicated passenger holding areas, known as Yatri Suvidha Kendras, at major railway stations across the country. This is being done to streamline passenger movement and ease congestion during periods of heavy footfall, including the festive season. The Yatri Suvidha Kendras, or Passenger Holding Areas, are being developed to provide dedicated space for unticketed and waiting passengers. Our correspondent reports that the facilities have been designed to ensure orderly passenger movement and provide a comfortable waiting environment.The holding areas have been designed to accommodate passengers before they proceed to the platform area. Talking to Akashvani News, Northern Railway CPRO  said that at New Delhi Railway station, a holding area is available for both reserved and unreserved classes. He said additional RPF personnel have also been deployed at Railway stations to facilitate passengers.At Anand Vihar Terminal, the Yatri Suvidha Kendra has 14 ticket counters, 16 CCTV cameras, four electronic display boards and seating for 20 passengers. The facility also has separate toilet facilities for male and female passengers, a Divyangjan toilet, an RO plant, 11 HVLS fans and a public announcement system. The aim is to reduce congestion on platforms, in circulating areas and at station approaches by providing designated spaces for waiting and ticketing.

. International Master Anuj Shrivatri of Madhya Pradesh has won the 7th ASEAN Plus Individual Open Chess Championship in Philippines to become India’s 100th Grandmaster and the first from his state to achieve the title. Shrivatri secured the title after scoring seven points from his final eight games, following a defeat in the opening round. The achievement was particularly significant as chess enthusiasts in India had been awaiting the country’s 100th Grandmaster, while Madhya Pradesh had been waiting for its first player to earn the prestigious title.All India Chess Federation President Nitin Narang has congratulated Anuj Shrivatri on becoming India’s 100th Grandmaster. He described the achievement as a historic milestone and a proud moment for Indian chess, expressing hope that the country would reach 200 Grandmasters next.

. Three major works of India’s literary and intellectual heritage including Kalhana’s Rajatarangini, the Mahabharata and Kautilya’s Arthashastra have been included in UNESCO’s Memory of the World Regional Register for Asia and the Pacific. The decision was taken at the 11th session of the register held in Jakarta, Indonesia. With this recognition, India’s total number of inscriptions in the regional register has risen to six. The three works represent different aspects of India’s knowledge traditions. Rajatarangini is a historical account of Kashmir, the Mahabharata explores Dharma, duty and human values, while Arthashastra deals with governance, diplomacy and statecraft. This recognition is a matter of pride for India’s civilisational continuity, its rich knowledge traditions and its contribution to the world. The development was announced by Member Secretary, Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA),  Dr. Sachchidanand Joshi which played an important role in preparing the nomination dossiers for all three works.

. In the forex market today,  the rupee depreciated marginally to trade at 93.94 rupees against the US dollar.The dollar index, which indicates US dollar’s strength against a basket of six other leading currencies, was trading at 101.82 in intra-day trade.

. Indian Railways has announced 1,265 vacancies for Station Master posts across various Railway Recruitment Boards and zones, opening up new employment opportunities for graduate candidates. The Railways Ministry said that in an important recruitment-related decision, the Railway Board has prescribed that Station Master recruitment will be notified separately from 2026 onwards. The dedicated recruitment process provides candidates with a specific notification covering eligibility requirements, examination procedures and vacancy distribution for the post. The online application window will remain open till 25th of next month. Candidates are advised to review the detailed eligibility conditions, vacancy distribution and application instructions before submitting their forms. The recruitment reflects Indian Railways’ continued efforts to provide career opportunities to eligible candidates while strengthening its operational workforce.

. Indian shuttlers Tushar Suveer and Rakshitha Ramraj clinched the men’s and women’s singles titles, at the Telangana India International Challenge 2026 today.India won three of the five titles. The top-seeded men’s doubles pair of Krishna Prasad Garaga and Pruthvi Krishnamurthy Roy also claimed victory, defeating compatriots Sai Pratheek K and Ruban Kumar Rethinasabapathi 21-12, 21-18.In the men’s singles final, sixth seed Tushar defeated compatriot Bharat Raghav 15-21, 21-18, 21-19.Top seed Rakshitha also emerged victorious in the women’s singles final, beating ninth seed Rujula Ramu 16-21, 21-15, 21-14.India narrowly missed out on a fourth title when Sathish Kumar Karunakaran and Ashwini Ponnappa lost the mixed doubles final to Russia’s Rodion Alimov and Alina Davletova 19-21, 21-11, 21-13.Japan’s Mei Sudo and Mai Tanabe won the women’s doubles title, defeating Thailand’s Phattharin Aiamvareesrisakul and Sarisa Janpeng 21-11, 21-11.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi held a telephone conversation with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy yesterday.During the conversation, President Zelenskyy shared his perspective on the latest developments related to the ongoing conflict. During the telephonic conversation, Prime Minister reaffirmed India’s human-centric approach and reiterated India’s consistent position that the conflict must be resolved through dialogue and diplomacy. Mr Modi conveyed India’s readiness to contribute to all efforts aimed at peaceful resolution of the conflict.The two leaders also discussed measures to further strengthen India-Ukraine bilateral cooperation in various sectors for the mutual benefit of the people of both countries.

. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian has said that Tehran is open to dialogue and negotiations but would not give in to pressure or coercion. Pezeshkian in an event yesterday in Tehran asserted that any negotiations must take place based on justice and equal terms. He said, Iran can talk with dignity and end the issue with dignity, but will not surrender to force and bullying. Mr. Pezeshkian referred to his address at the United Nations General Assembly in September, reiterating that Iran was willing to pursue diplomatic engagement based on fairness and mutual respect.

. Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment Dr Virendra Kumar today inaugurated the Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 at Dilli Haat, INA in New Delhi this evening. The Mela will provide a dedicated marketing platform to artisans and beneficiaries belonging to Scheduled Castes, Other Backward Classes, Safai Karamcharis and persons with disabilities to showcase and market their products to a wider audience. Speaking on the occassion, Dr Kumar said the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment has been organising Shilp Samagam Melas since 2022 and more than 1,000 artisans from Scheduled Castes, Other Backward Classes and Safai Karamcharis have benefited from opportunities to exhibit and market their products.  The Minister said that with approximately 150 stalls for participating male and female artisans to showcase their handicraft and handloom products under Bharat TULIP and Purple Fest, the initiative brings traditional artisans, creative talent and persons with disabilities together on a common platform to encourage wider market access and equal opportunities for participation.  The Mela will remain open to visitors until 15th of this month.

. Bringing festive cheer to Dalal Street, both the National Stock Exchange and the Bombay Stock Exchange will host the special Diwali Muhurat Trading session today.According to the circulars released by the exchanges, the markets will open at 2:20 PM and close at 3:30 PM. The one-hour session also marks the beginning of the new Hindu financial year, Vikram Samvat 2083, and coincides with Diwali celebrations. All trades executed during this session will carry normal settlement obligations.

. In the bullion market, gold and silver prices rebounded last week. The rise was supported by steep decline in crude oil prices over hopes of policy shifts following the US midterm elections. Meanwhile, concerns surrounding the global artificial intelligence sector also drove sharp flows from equity markets to commodity markets.At the Multi Commodity Exchange (MCX), Gold futures for December contract gained nearly 2.7 percent to settle at 1 lakh 42 thousand 167 rupees per 10 grams during the week. Silver futures for December contract rose almost 3.2 percent to close at 1 lakh 84 thousand 787 rupees per kilogram.Meanwhile, at the Commodity Exchange (COMEX), Gold futures for the December contract jumped 4.5 percent during the week to settle at 4,074.9 dollars per troy ounce. Silver futures for the December contract climbed 5.4 percent over the week to end at 51.94 dollars per troy ounce.

. The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) Women’s Selection Committee has announced squads for the upcoming all-format tour of South Africa in December. Smriti Mandhana is set to lead the side across all three formats.India will play one Test, three ODIs and three T20Is during the tour, which will begin with the Test match in Gqeberha on 9th December. The ODI series will start on 16th December in Paarl, followed by the second match in Cape Town on 19th December and the third in Bloemfontein on 22nd December. The three-match T20I series will begin on December 26 in Benoni. The second and third matches are scheduled to be played in Potchefstroom.Deepti Sharma has been named vice-captain of the Test and ODI squads, while Shafali Verma will serve as vice-captain in the T20I format. The Test squad features 15 players, including Harmanpreet Kaur, Jemimah Rodrigues, Richa Ghosh, Yastika Bhatia, Sneh Rana and Kranti Gaud. The ODI squad also comprises 15 players, with Vaishnavi Sharma included in place of Sneh Rana from the Test squad. The T20I squad has 17 players, with Shafali Verma as vice-captain. Niki Prasad, G. Kamalini, Anushka Sharma, Prema Rawat, Amanjot Kaur, Renuka Singh Thakur and Arundhati Reddy are also part of the squad.

. The nationwide ‘Viksit Bharat Yuva Samvad: Know Your Vote’ campaign has concluded with 536 Yuva Samvads conducted across 31 States and Union Territories. The campaign organised by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports through Mera Yuva Bharat (MY Bharat) reached over one lakh young people and involved more than 5000 Youth Icons. The campaign brought discussions on electoral awareness to colleges and educational institutions across the country. It encouraged young people, particularly first-time voters, to understand their voting rights and electoral procedures and participate responsibly in democracy.The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports said that the campaign witnessed participation by Governors, Union Ministers, State Ministers, Members of Parliament and other public representatives. It added that sports personalities and youth icons from the sporting community also participated in programmes, sharing their experiences and encouraging youth participation in sports.The Yuva Samvads provided young participants with opportunities to seek clarity on electoral procedures, discuss voting rights and civic responsibilities, and interact directly with public representatives and Youth Icons.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices ended in positive zone today. The Sensex rose 107 points or 0.13 per cent to close at 81,107. The Nifty gained 58 points or 0.23 per cent to settle at 25,045. In the broader market on the National Stock Exchange, the Midcap 100 index added 0.6 per cent and the Smallcap 100 index rose marginally.

. Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) have turned net buyers of Indian equities during the first week of November. According to the latest depository data, FPIs have invested 38,971 crore rupees in the domestic stock market, marking a reversal in investment flows. Of the total investment, 38 thousand 519 crore rupees came through purchases on stock exchanges, while 452 crore rupees were invested through the primary market.The shift in FPI’s sentiment was due to sharp sell-off in global technology stocks, triggered by concerns over artificial intelligence-related investments and a possible slowdown in data centre spending. The recent correction in global AI stocks has made Indian equities more attractive to overseas investors.Meanwhile, the debt market witnessed net inflows of 4,319 crore rupees in November so far.

A group of Chinese nationals have been livestreaming from low-income neighbourhoods in Dhaka for several months, allegedly presenting the locations as parts of New Delhi, India, according to reports in Bangladeshi media. The activity has been reported mainly in Sector 12 of Uttara, Dhaka and the nearby Tekpara area, where local residents estimate that more than 150 Chinese nationals are involved in filming streets, markets and residential areas of Dhaka.According to a report by Bangladeshi newspapers the livestreamers carry two mobile phones and record videos throughout the day. Some have reportedly entered people’s homes to film, raising concerns among residents over privacy and unauthorised recording.An analysis of the Chinese-language broadcasts, translated and verified by four Bangladeshis familiar with the language, reportedly found that some livestreamers described their location as New Delhi while making derogatory remarks about local residents and living conditions. The activities have raised questions among residents about the purpose of the livestreams, the use of recorded footage and the privacy of local communities.

. 81 year old British author M John Harrison was named the winner of the 2026 Booker Prize for his dystopian satire ‘The End of Everything’ at a ceremony in London last night. Harrison becomes the oldest author to win the prestigious literary prize after a writing career spanning 60 years.Just 198 pages, ‘The End of Everything’ was also the shortest novel on this year’s shortlist and won because judges felt it is a book that leaves you with a twinge of optimism about the world.Fiction authors from the UK dominated the shortlist of the 2026 Booker. Elizabeth Strout for ‘The Things We Never Say’, ‘Black Bag’ by Luke Kennard and ‘May We Feed the King’ by Rebecca Perry were  among the finalists.

. In Men’s Cricket, rain and wet outfield has delayed the start of the third ODI between India and hosts New Zealand at Seddon Park in Hamilton. The match was originally scheduled to begin at 7:30 AM Indian Standard Time. However, persistent rain and a wet outfield delayed the toss.India have already won first two games of the series in Auckland and Wellington. Another victory would give India an unassailable lead with two games remaining.The hosts need a win in Hamilton to stay in contention, while India have the opportunity to settle the contest with two matches still to play. The 4th ODI between India and New Zealand is scheduled for Friday.

. Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has left Dhaka on a three-day official visit to Türkiye to attend the COP31 World Leaders’ Summit in Antalya on November 11 and 12. During the summit, Mr Rahman will address the plenary session on November 12 and outline Bangladesh’s position on climate justice, climate finance, adaptation and compensation for loss and damage caused by climate change. Despite contributing only 0.05 per cent of global greenhouse gas emissions, Bangladesh remains one of the countries most vulnerable to climate change.On the sidelines of the summit, Mr Rahman is expected to hold bilateral meetings with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, the Australian Prime Minister, the President of Uzbekistan and the British Foreign Secretary. Discussions are likely to focus on trade, investment, climate cooperation and bilateral relations.Bangladesh will also showcase jute as an eco-friendly alternative to plastic through a dedicated pavilion in the conference’s Green Zone. Two special events will highlight the vulnerability of women to climate change and the potential of biodegradable jute products.

. Union Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways Sarbananda Sonowal today launched a recreational river cruise service along the Yamuna in New Delhi. The cruise named Namo Yamuna River Safari will cover a six-kilometres area along the river Yamuna between Sonia Vihar-Jagatpur. The ticket price for the cruise service is 500 rupees per person, while entry ticket to the premises will cost 50 rupees. Speaking on the occasion, Mr Sonowal said that the Delhi government is committed to cleaning the Yamuna and making its water beneficial for people’s lives.Delhi Chief Minister Rekah Gupta said that for the first time the people of Delhi will experience the Cruise Service named as Namo Yamuna River Safari. She invited the people of Delhi to experience the cruise service with their family members which provides a positive image of the national capital Delhi.  Mrs Gupta added that Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has implemented projects worth over one lakh and 25 thousand crore rupees in the national capital to decongest the city. The Chief Minister said that the BJP-led Delhi government is committed to working in the interest of the people. Akashvani correspondent reports that the newly introduced cruise service offers visitors a six-kilometres round-trip experience between Sonia Vihar-Jagatpur.The initiative aims to promote river-based tourism and offer visitors a new recreational experience in the national capital. The facilities at the site will include a musical fountain, a children’s play zone, shopping facilities, a food court and adventure sports activities. The development of the recreational river cruise service in Delhi marks an important step towards harnessing the potential of this National Waterway for recreational navigation and river-based tourism. The initiative is expected to offer Delhi residents and tourists a unique experience while fostering greater public engagement with the Yamuna. The use of electric-powered cruise vessels will also add a new recreational attraction to the National Capital Region.
